name: Section Inventory
instruction: Build a complete catalog of every node in the section before extracting any styles. This catalog drives the extraction - if a node is not in the catalog, it will not be extracted, and the output will be wrong.

actions.note: Scale 2 for text readability. This is the ground truth image. Save it mentally - every built component gets compared against it.
Depth 10 to reach every leaf. If '... N children' appears, that subtree was truncated - call get_tree_summary on that node specifically to expand it.

actions.instruction: For every node in the tree summary that shows '... N children' (truncated), call get_tree_summary on that node with depth 10. Repeat until every leaf node is visible. Do not proceed to extraction until the full tree is known.
Produce a flat list of every node ID in the section, grouped by depth level. This is the extraction manifest.
actions.rule: If a node appears in the tree summary, it appears in the catalog. No exceptions. Text nodes, SVG elements, dividers, dots, icons - everything.

actions.instruction: For complex sections with multiple visual groups, screenshot each top-level child frame separately at scale 2. This gives higher-resolution reference images for detailed areas like cards, lists, or panels.
actions.when: section has more than 3 top-level children or is taller than 800px

actions.instruction: Compare each child's x position and width against the section frame's content box (width minus paddingInline). A child is an overflow region when x + width > section content box width, or when the child's x offset puts its right edge past the section's right boundary. Record these as 'bleed nodes' in the catalog - they require margin offset + overflow: clip on the wrapping container. Common pattern: a dashboard or card strip offset rightward to create a 'bleeds off the edge' effect where the right side is cropped.
actions.method: For each direct child from get_children, compare child.x + child.width against section.width. If it exceeds by more than 2px, flag it as a bleed node. Also check if a child's x offset is significantly larger than the section's paddingInline - this means it is pushed rightward relative to siblings.

output_fields.bleed_nodes: list of node IDs that overflow the section boundary horizontally
output_fields.offset_nodes: list of node IDs with x offset > section paddingInline (shifted right or left of the normal content flow)
output_fields.abs_overflow_nodes: list of absolutely positioned nodes whose top + height exceeds their parent container's height. These require extra padding-bottom on the section to prevent clipping.

output.screenshot: Reference image of the full section
output.node_catalog: Flat list of every node ID grouped by depth
output.bleed_nodes: Node IDs that extend past the section boundary (require overflow: clip)
output.offset_nodes: Node IDs with non-standard x offset (require margin-left adjustment)
